sections.title: Who wins when ideas aren't secret

items.q: Is there still proprietary AI technology that no rival can access?
items.a: Panel view for 2026: **no** — researchers rotate; ideas aren't proprietary long-term. Differentiation is **budget, hardware, culture, and product integration**, not secret architectures.

items.q: What did the DeepSeek moment change?
items.a: **DeepSeek R1 (Jan 2025)** kicked off a Chinese open-weight explosion; Kimi, MiniMax, and Z.ai leapfrog while DeepSeek stays slightly ahead. Labs release open weights for **influence + global distribution** (US enterprises won't pay Chinese API subs).

sections.title: Architecture vs where gains actually live

items.q: How different is today's architecture from GPT-2?
items.a: Still the **same decoder-only lineage** — MoE, GQA, MLA, sliding window are **incremental tweaks**. Turbulence is in **training stages, data quality, and systems** (e.g. FP8 → ~**30% faster** training).

**No** — but compute is **reallocated**. Pre-training still helps; **RLVR and test-time compute** currently offer better bang-for-buck than bigger pre-training alone. Key distinction: **RLVR scales**; **RLHF doesn't** (reward-model over-optimization ceiling).

items.q: What are the three stages of LLM training?
items.a: **Pre-training** (next-token on curated/synthetic mix) → **mid-training** (long-context, quality, forgetting mitigation) → **post-training** (SFT, DPO, RLVR, RLHF). **Data quality > raw scale** (OLMo 3: less data, better mix).

items.q: Which coding harnesses does the panel actually use?
items.a: Sebastian: **Codeium in VS Code**; Nathan: **Claude Code** for "programming with English"; Lex: **half Cursor / half Claude Code**. Claude Code is called a **better utilization of Opus 4.5** than the same model side-by-side in Cursor/VS Code.

items.q: What's still hard about agents in 2026?
items.a: **Computer-use demos still suck** (Operator, Claude computer use) — harder than backend API tools; specification/interface is the blocker. Tool use **reduces hallucinations** but doesn't solve them. Expect long context at **2–5M tokens**, not 100M.

sections.title: AGI, jobs, and what actually matters

items.a: Expect **jagged intelligence** — superhuman at frontend/traditional ML; weak at distributed training, safety-critical systems, Chrome-scale complexity. Trend: humans → **system designers / PMs**; fewer humans per useful line of code, not zero soon. **"You can outsource thinking, but not understanding."**

items.q: What impact does the panel think is understated vs GDP leaps?
items.a: **Making all human knowledge accessible globally.** The "one model to rule everything" dream is fading toward specialized models and integrations — expect **amplification for years**, not a clean paradigm change. AI 2027 ASI milestones get pushed toward ~**2031** with skepticism.
